transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um, I hope I'm not wasting your time, but I came in because... well, I've been having a bit of a hard time lately. It’s probably just something I need to try harder at, but whenever I’m supposed to sit still—like in my classes or when I'm in the radiology suite—I get this feeling like I’m just crawling out of my skin. I’ve really been trying to tough it out for months, I promise I have, but I always just end up pacing around, or shifting constantly, or trying to find some excuse to get up and move. 

I just can't seem to stop doing it, even when I know I'm supposed to be quiet and still. Is that... does that make sense as a reason to come see you?
When you feel like you need to get up and move, do you also feel anxious?

Oh, um... no, I don't think I do. I really hope I'm explaining this right, but I don't feel worried or nervous when it happens. It's not like a panic thing at all. 

It's more just... my body just really, really wants to go. Like there's a motor inside me that won't turn off, and I just have to burn off the energy somehow. Mentally I feel totally fine, just... physically restless, I guess? I'm sorry if that's not a very helpful answer. Does that make sense for what you're asking?
Since you were a child, have you often had trouble paying attention or staying seated when you were expected to?

Um, yeah... I guess so. I really hope it doesn't make me sound like I was a bad kid, because I always wanted to be good and do the right thing! But, um, my parents actually still bring up my old elementary school conferences. They said my teachers would always mention how I was constantly out of my seat, or calling out, or rushing ahead to do things before the directions were even finished. 

So, yeah, I guess that kind of stuff was happening way before middle school, not just recently with my radiology training. I think I was just a really eager kid, mostly? I hope it's okay that I shared that... is that the kind of background information you were looking for?
